newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico rebels say yet to unleash full armed power.
newsitem.headline: Mexico rebels say yet to unleash full armed power.

text.p: Mexico's Marxist guerrillas have yet to unleash their full military power on their main enemy, the country's "financial oligarchy", rebel chiefs said in an interview published on Thursday by La Jornada newspaper.

Three masked commanders from the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) -- one of them a woman identified as Victoria -- spoke during a clandestine conversation with six journalists in a guerrilla safe house, apparently in Mexico City, the newspaper said. It published photographs of the encounter.

The EPR first appeared last June in the southwestern state of Guerrero but has since attacked in at least five central and southern states. Police estimate the group has killed about 30 people while the guerrillas claim over 90 victims.
In the interview, an EPR leader named Comandante Oscar mocked government attempts to hunt down his guerrillas.
"They are like a big elephant trying to hunt a small animal (which is) more agile", he said, as a dozen EPR rebels armed with submachine guns stood guard.
Only three of the people arrested by police as EPR sympathisers were actually members of the group, he said.
Left-wing groups complain that more than 200 innocent activists have been arrested on trumped-up EPR charges. The government says around 90 genuine suspects have been detained.
"We have not yet activated our full capacity from a military point of view," Oscar said. "The places where actions have been carried out are part of a plan, a strategy.

"The main enemy we are facing is the financial oligarchy linked with big transnational financial capital. Our actions are directed against the pillars of that oligarchy, the armed forces of the country, the police", he added.

An EPR unit in Guerrero said in an interview last week with foreign media that the group might try a spectacular attack like the one staged by Peru's Marxist Tupac Amaru guerrillas when they stormed the Japanese embassy residence last December and took more than 400 hostages.
But Oscar said: "We have not yet declared war because we believe that corresponds to another degree of development."
